title: Thirty minutes in the bath
setting: A cold evening at Kenta and Sora's flat. Kenta is cooking dinner when Sora gets home from his shift at the café.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.ja: ただいま。ああ、外めっちゃ寒かった。
lines.kana: ただいま。ああ、そとめっちゃさむかった。
lines.english: I'm home. Ugh, it's freezing out there.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: okaeri. gohan, mou sugu dekiru yo.
lines.ja: おかえり。ご飯、もうすぐできるよ。
lines.kana: おかえり。ごはん、もうすぐできるよ。

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, kenta ga gohan tsukutte kureteru no? arigatou!
lines.ja: え、ケンタがご飯作ってくれてるの？ありがとう！
lines.kana: え、けんたがごはんつくってくれてるの？ありがとう！
lines.english: Oh, you're making dinner for me? Thanks!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un, hanbaagu. boku mo mada gohan tabetenai n da.
lines.ja: うん、ハンバーグ。僕もまだご飯食べてないんだ。
lines.kana: うん、はんばーぐ。ぼくもまだごはんたべてないんだ。
lines.english: Yep, hamburger steak. I haven't eaten yet either.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, demo, chotto ofuro haitte kite ii? samukute.
lines.ja: あ、でも、ちょっとお風呂入ってきていい？寒くて。
lines.kana: あ、でも、ちょっとおふろはいってきていい？さむくて。
lines.english: Oh, but can I hop in the bath first? I'm frozen.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: え、今？ご飯冷めちゃうよ。
lines.kana: え、いま？ごはんさめちゃうよ。
lines.english: What, now? The food'll get cold.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ、すぐでるから！

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sora, mou sanjuppun da yo! gohan, samechatta yo.
lines.ja: ソラ、もう三十分だよ！ご飯、冷めちゃったよ。
lines.kana: そら、もうさんじゅっぷんだよ！ごはん、さめちゃったよ。
lines.english: Sora, it's been thirty minutes! The food's gone cold.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.ja: ごめんごめん！お風呂、気持ちよくて。
lines.kana: ごめんごめん！おふろ、きもちよくて。
lines.english: Sorry, sorry! The bath just felt so good.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: もういいから、ご飯食べよう。
lines.kana: もういいから、ごはんたべよう。

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ano ne, kenta. boku, mou gohan tabete kichatta.
lines.ja: あのね、ケンタ。僕、もうご飯食べてきちゃった。
lines.kana: あのね、けんた。ぼく、もうごはんたべてきちゃった。
lines.english: Um, Kenta? I kind of already ate before I came home.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e? nande ima iu no? gohan tsukutta noni.
lines.ja: え？なんで今言うの？ご飯作ったのに。
lines.kana: え？なんでいまいうの？ごはんつくったのに。
lines.english: What? Why are you only telling me now? I made dinner!

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: demo, kenta no gohan wa taberu yo! itadakimasu!
lines.ja: でも、ケンタのご飯は食べるよ！いただきます！
lines.kana: でも、けんたのごはんはたべるよ！いただきます！
lines.english: But I'm still eating your cooking! Itadakimasu!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: おなかいっぱいじゃないの？
lines.kana: おなかいっぱいじゃないの？

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, ippai. demo, n! samete mo oishii!
lines.ja: うん、いっぱい。でも、ん！冷めてもおいしい！
lines.kana: うん、いっぱい。でも、ん！さめてもおいしい！
lines.english: Yeah, stuffed. But... mm! It's good even cold!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ashita wa sora ga gohan tsukutte ne. gohan dekitara, boku wa sugu iku kara.
lines.ja: 明日はソラがご飯作ってね。ご飯できたら、僕はすぐ行くから。
lines.kana: あしたはそらがごはんつくってね。ごはんできたら、ぼくはすぐいくから。
lines.english: Tomorrow, you're making dinner. And the second it's ready, I'll be right there.

choices.english: Kenta cooks dinner, but Sora takes a long bath and it goes cold. Then Sora admits he has already eaten, but he eats Kenta's food anyway.
Sora cooks dinner for Kenta, but Kenta takes a long bath and the food goes cold.
Kenta cooks dinner, but Sora has already eaten, so he goes to bed and Kenta eats alone.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-4: Kenta is making dinner (gohan, mou sugu dekiru yo; kenta ga gohan tsukutte kureteru no?). Line 5: Sora wants a bath first, and in line 10, thirty minutes later, the food has gone cold (gohan, samechatta yo). Line 13: Sora admits he already ate before coming home (mou gohan tabete kichatta), but in lines 15 and 17 he eats anyway (kenta no gohan wa taberu yo! ... samete mo oishii!). B swaps the two: Kenta is the one cooking and Sora is the one in the bath. C is wrong: Sora doesn't go to bed. He sits down and eats Kenta's dinner even though he's full (line 17: un, ippai. demo...).

questions.english: Kenta asks you, "ne, mou gohan tabeta?" (Hey, have you eaten yet?) You haven't eaten yet. Tell him.
questions.answer: Say not yet, using mada and the negative of taberu's -teru form: uun, mada gohan tabetenai. Don't say tabenakatta: that means you skipped the meal.

modelAnswers.ja: ううん、まだご飯食べてない。

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, gohan mada tabetenai n da. onaka suita yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、ご飯まだ食べてないんだ。おなかすいたよ。
modelAnswers.english: No, I haven't had dinner yet. I'm starving.

questions.explanation: gohan is any meal, not only rice: in this scene Kenta's gohan is hamburger steak (line 4). For 'not yet', Japanese uses mada with the negative -teru form, exactly as Kenta says in line 4 (boku mo mada gohan tabetenai n da). tabenakatta would mean you didn't eat the meal at all, not that you haven't got to it yet. If you had already eaten, you'd say un, tabeta, or, like Sora in line 13, mou gohan tabete kichatta (I already ate before I got here).

questions.english: At the end, Kenta says, "ashita wa sora ga gohan tsukutte ne." What does he want Sora to do tomorrow?
questions.ja: ケンタは明日、ソラに何をしてほしいですか？
questions.kana: けんたはあした、そらになにをしてほしいですか？
questions.romaji: kenta wa ashita, sora ni nani o shite hoshii desu ka?

choices.english: Cook just the rice, while Kenta makes the rest of the meal.
Come straight home after work so they can eat together.
Make dinner for the two of them.

questions.explanation: gohan tsukuru means 'cook a meal, make dinner': tomorrow Sora cooks, the way Kenta did tonight (line 14: gohan tsukutta noni, 'I made dinner!'). A is the rice trap: gohan here is the whole meal, and tonight's was hamburger steak. Cooking just the rice would be gohan o taku. B: Kenta says nothing about Sora coming home. His jab comes in the next sentence: gohan dekitara, boku wa sugu iku kara (the second dinner's ready, I'll be right there), unlike Sora and his thirty-minute bath.

questions.english: While Sora is in the bath, Kenta finishes cooking and calls out to him. What does he shout?
questions.ja: ケンタは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta wa nan to iimashita ka?
questions.explanation: Line 8: sora! gohan dekita yo! The kitchen call uses dekiru in the past: the meal has been made, so it's ready. A is what you get by translating 'ready' with junbi. Japanese would say gohan no junbi ga dekita, which still uses dekiru, and the everyday call is simply gohan dekita yo. C, gohan owatta, means the meal is over and everyone has finished eating, which is the opposite moment. Notice the tense: in line 2 Kenta said mou sugu dekiru yo. Non-past dekiru means it'll be ready very soon, not that it's ready now.

questions.english: Dinner is hot on the table. Sora says, "jaa, chotto ofuro haitte kuru ne." (Right, I'm just going to hop in the bath.) Tell him the food will get cold.
questions.ja: じゃあ、ちょっとお風呂入ってくるね。
questions.kana: じゃあ、ちょっとおふろはいってくるね。
questions.romaji: jaa, chotto ofuro haitte kuru ne.
questions.answer: Warn him using the -chau form of sameru: e, ima? gohan samechau yo. Not samuku naru: samui is for the weather and for how a person feels.

modelAnswers.ja: え、今？ご飯冷めちゃうよ。
modelAnswers.english: What, now? The food'll get cold.

modelAnswers.romaji: gohan samechau kara, tabete kara ni shite yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ご飯冷めちゃうから、食べてからにしてよ。
modelAnswers.english: The food'll get cold, so have your bath after you eat.

questions.explanation: When hot food loses its heat, the verb is sameru. samechau adds 'and that would be a shame', which is why it's the usual warning. Kenta says it in line 6, and half an hour later he says it in the past in line 10 (gohan, samechatta yo). In the same scene Sora says samukatta and samukute (lines 1 and 5). That's samui, used for the cold weather outside and for how he feels, never for food. In line 17 Sora even eats the food cold: samete mo oishii (it's good even cold).

newWords.english: I'm home (said when you get home)
welcome back (said to someone getting home)
